scripts.radio:
Good evening, and welcome to Kenyans Are Asking.

This week, our national story sits between grand economic figures and harsh ground realities. On paper, Kenya remains East Africa’s largest economy, crossing the 115 billion dollar GDP mark. Yet across our 47 counties, enterprise is stalling. County governments currently hold over 107 billion shillings in unpaid pending bills. These are not mere statistics; they represent local contractors, food suppliers, and small family businesses running broke, with auctioneers at their gates because devolved units refuse to settle genuine debts.

Accountability, however, scored a major victory in the courts. Former Nairobi Provincial Commissioner Davis Chelogoi has been convicted over a 1.35 billion shilling prime land fraud in Westlands. For years, powerful administrators treated land registries as private playgrounds. This conviction is a vital signal to land grabbers that institutional memory and persistence can outlast executive impunity.

On a positive note for public healthcare, the North Rift has received a substantial boost as the 350-bed Kitale Referral Hospital begins offering critical specialized care, reducing the grueling journey patients previously made to Eldoret.

Kwa ufupi: Ingawa uchumi wa taifa umefikisha dola bilioni 115, madeni ya kaunti ya shilingi bilioni 107 yanaendelea kulemaza biashara ndogondogo. Wakati huo huo, kutiwa hatiani kwa aliyekuwa PC Davis Chelogoi kwa wizi wa ardhi ya bilioni 1.35 kunathibitisha kwamba sheria haina mkubwa. Ni wajibu wetu kuendelea kuuliza maswali na kuwawajibisha viongozi.
scripts.voice_note:
Habari zenu. Here is your quick update from Kenyans Are Asking.

Two contrasting numbers stood out this week: 115 billion dollars and 107 billion shillings. The first is our GDP, confirming Kenya as the region's economic giant. The second is what our county governments owe ordinary suppliers in pending bills. When counties fail to pay, small businesses shut down and families suffer. Find out what your county owes and ask your MCA why those bills are pending.

In the courts, former Nairobi PC Davis Chelogoi was convicted over a 1.35 billion shilling land fraud case in Westlands. A reminder that title deed integrity matters—never cut corners on due diligence.

Finally, the debate on the mandatory housing levy continues across the country: scrap it or retain it? Share your thoughts with us.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: Buying land? Never trust verbal claims or photocopied titles from brokers. Always conduct an official search at the Lands Registry before paying.
scripts.reels: For years, prime land in Nairobi seemed fair game for well-connected officials. Not anymore. Former Nairobi Provincial Commissioner Davis Chelogoi has been convicted over a 1.35 billion shilling land fraud case in Westlands. This conviction is a massive win for land justice in Kenya. It proves that public office cannot shield anyone from accountability. Justice may take time, but the law finally caught up.
